title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 66 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 439–441 (Night 66, continuing directly from nights-65), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 66 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Nuzhat al-Zamān, still unrecognised by her brother Sharkān in the presence of the four judges and the merchant, goes on with her anecdotes of the pious and the just: the letter of the caliph ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz to the pilgrims, his refusal to leave his twelve sons a fortune, and Khālid ibn Ṣafwān's warning to Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, told through the story of a king who laid down his crown. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالسِّتُّونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu wa-al-sittūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the sixth and the sixty,
sentences.i: And when it was the sixty-sixth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ قَالَتْ لِأَخِيهَا شَرْكَانَ وَهِيَ لَمْ تَعْرِفْهُ بِحُضُورِ الْقُضَاةِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ وَالتَّاجِرِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Nuzhata al-Zamāni qālat li-akhīhā Sharkāna wa-hiya lam taʿrifhu bi-ḥuḍūri al-quḍāti al-arbaʿati wa-al-tājiri
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate, that Nuzhat al-Zamān said to her brother Sharkān — and she had not recognised him — in the presence of the four judges and the merchant:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Nuzhat al-Zamān spoke to her brother Sharkān, though she did not know him for her brother, in the presence of the four judges and the merchant.
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and أن together (al-saʿīdu anna); kept as printed. The sentence picks up the tale from the previous night, where Nuzhat al-Zamān, sold as a slave girl, is telling Sharkān her stories of the wise and the pious without yet knowing who he is.

sentences.t: تَتِمَّةُ الْفَصْلِ الثَّانِي مِنَ الْبَابِ الْأَوَّلِ
sentences.tr: tatimmatu al-faṣli al-thānī mina al-bābi al-awwali
sentences.l: The completion of the second chapter of the first gate.
sentences.i: The rest of the second section of the first chapter.
sentences.n: A running heading in the print, not part of the speech: the anecdotes of the pious that Nuzhat al-Zamān is reciting are arranged in chapters, and this is the conclusion of the second section.

sentences.t: اتَّفَقَ أَنَّهُ كَتَبَ عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ إِلَى أَهْلِ الْمَوْسِمِ
sentences.tr: ittafaqa annahu kataba ʿUmaru ibnu ʿAbdi al-ʿAzīzi ilā ahli al-mawsimi
sentences.l: It happened that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to the people of the season.
sentences.i: It happened that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to the people of the pilgrimage season.
sentences.n: “The season” (al-mawsim) is the pilgrimage season at Mecca; the letter that follows was addressed to the pilgrims gathered there.

sentences.t: أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ فِى الشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ وَالْبَلَدِ الْحَرَامِ وَيَوْمِ الْحَجِّ الْأَكْبَرِ أَنِّي أَمْرُقُ مِنْ ظُلْمِكُمْ وَعُدْوَانِ مَنِ اعْتَدَى عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَمَرْتُ بِذَلِكَ أَوْ تَعَمَّدْتُهُ أَوْيَكُونَ أَمْرٌ مِنْ أُمُورِهِ بَلَغَنِي أَوْ أَحَاطَ بِهِ عِلْمِي وَأَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ لِذَلِكَ مَوْضِعًا عَنِ الْغُفْرَانِ
sentences.tr: ammā baʿdu fa-innī ushhidu Allāha fī al-shahri al-ḥarāmi wa-al-baladi al-ḥarāmi wa-yawmi al-ḥajji al-akbari annī amruqu min ẓulmikum wa-ʿudwāni mani iʿtadā ʿalaykum an akūna amartu bi-dhālika aw taʿammadtuhu awyakūna amrun min umūrihi balaghanī aw aḥāṭa bihi ʿilmī wa-arjū an yakūna li-dhālika mawḍiʿan ʿani al-ghufrāni
sentences.l: As for what follows: I call God to witness, in the sacred month and the sacred land and the day of the greater pilgrimage, that I go-out from your wronging and from the enmity of whoever transgressed against you — that I should have commanded that, or intended it, or that a matter of his matters should have reached me or my knowledge encompassed it; and I hope that for that there will be a place away from forgiveness.
sentences.i: To proceed: I call God to witness, in the sacred month, in the sacred land and on the day of the greater pilgrimage, that I am clear of any wrong done to you and of the aggression of anyone who has wronged you — that I commanded it, or meant it, or that any such matter ever reached me or came within my knowledge; and I hope that this will find a place for me in God's forgiveness.
sentences.n: Two forms here look like slips of the print. أمرق (“I go out from, I pass out of”) presumably stands for أبرأ (“I am clear of”), which is how the sense runs; it is read as printed. And the last phrase has عن (“away from”) where the sense wants من (“a place in forgiveness”); read as printed, and the idiomatic line gives the sense. The print also runs أو and يكون together (awyakūna). The letter opens with the formula أما بعد, “as for what follows,” the standard turn from greeting to business.

sentences.t: إِلَّا أَنَّهُ لَا إِذْنَ مِنِّي بِظُلْمِ أَحَدٍ فَإِنِّي مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ كُلِّ مَظْلُومٍ
sentences.tr: illā annahu lā idhna minnī bi-ẓulmi aḥadin fa-innī masʾūlun ʿan kulli maẓlūmin
sentences.l: Except that there is no permission from me for the wronging of anyone, for I am one-questioned about every wronged person.
sentences.i: But I have given no leave for anyone to be wronged, for I shall be called to account for every person wronged.

sentences.t: أَلَا وَأَيُّ عَامِلٍ مِنْ عُمَّالِي زَاغَ عَنِ الْحَقِّ وَعَمِلَ بِلَا كِتَابٍ وَلَا سُنَّةٍ فَلَا طَاعَةَ لَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَى الْحَقِّ
sentences.tr: alā wa-ayyu ʿāmilin min ʿummālī zāgha ʿani al-ḥaqqi wa-ʿamila bi-lā kitābin wa-lā sunnatin fa-lā ṭāʿata lahu ʿalaykum ḥattā yarjiʿa ilā al-ḥaqqi
sentences.l: Now then: and whichever governor of my governors has swerved from the truth and acted without Book and without custom, no obedience is due to him from you until he returns to the truth.
sentences.i: Hear this: any of my governors who strays from the truth and acts without the Book and the Sunna is owed no obedience from you until he returns to the truth.
sentences.n: Kitāb and sunna are the Qurʾān and the established practice of the Prophet, the two sources a Muslim ruler is bound by. أَلَا is the particle that calls attention.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ رَضِىَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يُخَفَّفَ عَنِّى الْمَوْتُ لِأَنَّهُ آخِرُ مَايُؤْجَرُ عَلَيْهِ الْمُؤْمِنُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu mā uḥibbu an yukhaffafa ʿannī al-mawtu li-annahu ākhiru mā yuʾjaru ʿalayhi al-muʾminu
sentences.l: And he said, God be pleased with him: I do not love that death be made light for me, because it is the last of what the believer is rewarded for.
sentences.i: And he said, God be pleased with him: I would not have death made easier for me, for it is the last thing for which a believer is rewarded.
sentences.n: Raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu, “God be pleased with him,” is the blessing said after the name of a Companion or a pious early figure. The print spells عنّي and رضي with final ى and runs ما and يؤجر together (mā yuʾjaru); kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ بَعْضُ الثِّقَاتِ قَدِمْتُ عَلَى أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ وَهُوَ خَلِيفَةٌ فَرَأَيْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ اثْنَىْ عَشَرَ دِرْهَمًا فَأَمَرَ بِوَضْعِهَا فِي بَيْتِ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla baʿḍu al-thiqāti qadimtu ʿalā amīri al-muʾminīna ʿUmara ibni ʿAbdi al-ʿAzīzi wa-huwa khalīfatun fa-raʾaytu bayna yadayhi ithnay ʿashara dirhaman fa-amara bi-waḍʿihā fī bayti al-māli
sentences.l: And one of the trustworthy said: I came to the commander of the believers ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he was caliph, and I saw between his hands twelve dirhams, and he commanded their placing in the house of the wealth.
sentences.i: And one of the trustworthy transmitters said: I came to the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, when he was caliph, and I saw twelve dirhams in front of him, and he ordered them put into the public treasury.
sentences.n: Al-thiqāt, “the trustworthy,” are reliable transmitters of reports; the phrase introduces a chain-less anecdote. The print spells اثنى with final ى. Bayt al-māl, “the house of wealth,” is the state treasury.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنَّكَ أَفْقَرْتَ أَوْلَادَكَ وَجَعَلْتَهُمْ عِيَالًا لَاشَيْءَ لَهُمْ فَلَوْ أَوْصَيْتَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِشَيْءٍ وَإِلَى مَنْ هُوَ فَقِيرٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِكَ
sentences.tr: qultu yā amīra al-muʾminīna innaka afqarta awlādaka wa-jaʿaltahum ʿiyālan lā shayʾa lahum fa-law awṣayta ilayhim bi-shayʾin wa-ilā man huwa faqīrun min ahli baytika
sentences.l: I said: O commander of the believers, you have impoverished your sons and made them dependants with nothing, so if only you had bequeathed to them something, and to whoever is poor of the people of your house —
sentences.i: I said: Commander of the Faithful, you have left your sons poor and made them dependants with nothing at all. If only you had left something to them, and to those of your household who are in need!
sentences.n: The print runs لا and شيء together (lā-shayʾ); kept as printed. The sentence breaks off after the wish, which is how the speaker puts it to the caliph.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ادْنُ مِنِّي فَدَنَوْتُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla udnu minnī fa-danawtu minhu
sentences.l: And he said: Draw near to me; and I drew near to him.
sentences.i: He said, “Come closer to me,” and I drew near to him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَمَّا قَوْلُكَ أَفْقَرْتَ أَوْلَادَكَ فَأَوْصِ إِلَيْهِمْ أَوْ إِنَى مَنْ هُوَ فَقِيرٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِكَ فَغَيْرُ سَدِيدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ammā qawluka afqarta awlādaka fa-awṣi ilayhim aw [ilā] man huwa faqīrun min ahli baytika fa-ghayru sadīdin
sentences.l: And he said: As for your saying, “You have impoverished your sons, so bequeath to them, or to whoever is poor of the people of your house,” it is not sound.
sentences.i: He said, “As for your saying that I have left my sons poor, and that I should have provided for them, or for those of my household in need — that is not sound,
sentences.n: The print has إنى where the sense wants إلى (ilā, “to”), a slip of the type; it is vocalised as printed and transliterated as the word it must be.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلِيفَتِي عَلَى أَوْلَادِي وَعَلَى مَنْ هُوَ فَقِيرٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِي وَهُوَ وَكِيلٌ عَلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: li-anna Allāha khalīfatī ʿalā awlādī wa-ʿalā man huwa faqīrun min ahli baytī wa-huwa wakīlun ʿalayhim
sentences.l: Because God is my successor over my sons and over whoever is poor of the people of my house, and He is an agent over them.
sentences.i: for God is my deputy over my sons and over every poor member of my household, and He is their guardian.

sentences.t: وَهُمْ مَا بَيْنَ رَجُلَيْنِ أَمَّا رَجُلٌ يَتَّقِى اللَّهَ فَسَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا وَأَمَّا رَجُلٌ مُعْتَكِفٌ عَلَى الْمَعَاصِي فَإِنِّي لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأُقَوِّيَهُ عَلَى مَعْصِيَةِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-hum mā bayna rajulayni ammā rajulun yattaqī Allāha fa-sa-yajʿalu Allāhu lahu makhrajan wa-ammā rajulun muʿtakifun ʿalā al-maʿāṣī fa-innī lam akun li-uqawwiyahu ʿalā maʿṣiyati Allāhi
sentences.l: And they are between two men: as for a man who fears God, God will make for him a way out; and as for a man given-up to acts of disobedience, I would not be one to strengthen him in disobeying God.
sentences.i: They will be one of two kinds of men. A man who fears God, God will make a way out for him; and a man who clings to sin, I will not be the one to strengthen him in disobedience to God.”
sentences.n: The first half echoes Qurʾān 65:2, “whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out.” Muʿtakif is the word for one who stays in retreat in a mosque; here it is turned to mean one who is devoted to, shut up in, his sins. The print writes the shadda on لأقوّيه.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعَثَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَأَحْضَرَهُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَكَانُوا اثْنَىْ عَشَرَ ذَكَرًا فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ ذَرَفَتْ عَيْنَاهُ بِالْبُكَاءِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿatha ilayhim wa-aḥḍarahum bayna yadayhi wa-kānū ithnay ʿashara dhakaran fa-lammā naẓara ilayhim dharafat ʿaynāhu bi-al-bukāʾi
sentences.l: Then he sent to them and had them brought between his hands, and they were twelve males; and when he looked at them his two eyes streamed with weeping.
sentences.i: Then he sent for his sons and had them brought before him — there were twelve boys — and when he looked at them his eyes overflowed with tears.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ إِنَّ أَبَاكُمْ مَا بَيْنَ أَمْرَيْنِ إِمَّا أَنْ تَسْتَغْنُوا فَيَدْخُلُ أَبُوكُمُ النَّارَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ تَفْتَقِرُوا فَيَدْخُلُ أَبُوكُمُ الْجَنَّةَ وَدُخُولُ أَبِيكُمُ الْجَنَّةَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ أَنْ تَسْتَغْنُوا قُومُوا عَصَمَكُمُ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla inna abākum mā bayna amrayni immā an tastaghnū fa-yadkhulu abūkumu al-nāra wa-immā an taftaqirū fa-yadkhulu abūkumu al-jannata wa-dukhūlu abīkumu al-jannata aḥabbu ilayhi min an tastaghnū qūmū ʿaṣamakumu Allāhu
sentences.l: Then he said: Truly your father is between two matters: either you become rich, and your father enters the Fire; or you become poor, and your father enters the Garden. And your father's entering the Garden is dearer to him than that you become rich. Rise — God protect you!
sentences.i: Then he said, “Your father stands between two outcomes: either you grow rich and your father enters the Fire, or you grow poor and your father enters Paradise. And your father's entering Paradise is dearer to him than your being rich. Go now, and may God protect you.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ وَكَلْتُ أَمْرَكُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qad wakaltu amrakum ilā Allāhi
sentences.l: For I have entrusted your affair to God.
sentences.i: I have left your affairs to God.”

sentences.t: وَقَالَ خَالِدُ بْنُ صَفْوَانَ صَحِبَنِي يُوسُفُ بْنُ عُمَرَ إِلَى هِشَامِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ فَلَمَّا قَدِمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَقَدْ خَرَجَ بِقَرَابَتِهِ وَخَدَمِهِ فَنَزَلَ فِي أَرْضٍ وَضُرِبَتْ لَهُ خَيْمَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla Khālidu ibnu Ṣafwāna ṣaḥibanī Yūsufu ibnu ʿUmara ilā Hishāmi ibni ʿAbdi al-Maliki fa-lammā qadimtu ʿalayhi wa-qad kharaja bi-qarābatihi wa-khadamihi fa-nazala fī arḍin wa-ḍuribat lahu khaymatun
sentences.l: And Khālid ibn Ṣafwān said: Yūsuf ibn ʿUmar accompanied me to Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik; and when I came to him — he had gone out with his kinsfolk and his servants and alighted in a land, and a tent was pitched for him —
sentences.i: Khālid ibn Ṣafwān said: Yūsuf ibn ʿUmar took me with him to Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik. When I came before him, he had ridden out with his kinsmen and servants and made camp in open country, and a tent had been pitched for him.
sentences.n: Khālid ibn Ṣafwān al-Tamīmī was a famous Basran orator at the Umayyad court, and Hishām (r. 724–743) the caliph; Yūsuf ibn ʿUmar al-Thaqafī was his governor of Iraq. The construction is loose, as often in Middle Arabic: the sentence begins “when I came to him” and the narration runs on without a main verb until the next sentence.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتِ النَّاسُ مَجَالِسَهُمْ خَرَجْتُ مِنْ نَاحِيَةِ الْبِسَاطِ فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَلَمَّا صَارَتْ عَيْنِي فِي عَيْنِهِ قُلْتُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā akhadhati al-nāsu majālisahum kharajtu min nāḥiyati al-bisāṭi fa-naẓartu ilayhi fa-lammā ṣārat ʿaynī fī ʿaynihi qultu lahu
sentences.l: And when the people (she) took their seats, I went out from the side of the carpet and looked at him; and when my eye came to be in his eye, I said to him:
sentences.i: When the people had taken their seats, I stepped out from the side of the carpet and looked at him, and when my eyes met his, I said to him,
sentences.n: Al-nās, “the people,” takes a feminine verb (أخذت) here; kept as printed, a common Middle Arabic agreement.

sentences.t: أَتَمَّ اللَّهُ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَجَعَلَ مَا قَلَّدَكَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمُورِ رَشَدًا وَلَا خَالَطَ سُرُورَكَ أَذًى وَلَمْ أَجِدْ لَكَ نَصِيحَةً يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَبْلَغَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ مَنْ سَلَفَ قَبْلَكَ مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: atamma Allāhu niʿmatahu ʿalayka yā amīra al-muʾminīna wa-jaʿala mā qalladaka min hādhihi al-umūri rashadan wa-lā khālaṭa surūraka adhan wa-lam ajid laka naṣīḥatan yā amīra al-muʾminīna ablagha min ḥadīthi man salafa qablaka mina al-mulūki
sentences.l: May God complete His favour upon you, O commander of the believers, and make what He has hung upon your neck of these affairs right guidance, and may no harm mix with your joy. And I have found for you no counsel, O commander of the believers, more eloquent than the tale of those kings who passed before you.
sentences.i: May God perfect His favour to you, Commander of the Faithful, and make the charge He has laid on you a guidance to right action, and let no harm mingle with your joy. I could find no counsel for you, Commander of the Faithful, more telling than the story of one of the kings who went before you.
sentences.n: The verbs are optative: “May God complete…”. Qallada is “to hang a necklace or sword-belt on someone,” hence to invest with an office.

sentences.t: فَاسْتَوَى جَالِسًا وَكَانَ مُتَّكِئًا وَقَالَ هَاتِ مَا عِنْدَكَ يَا ابْنَ صَفْوَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-istawā jālisan wa-kāna muttakiʾan wa-qāla hāti mā ʿindaka yā ibna Ṣafwāna
sentences.l: And he sat upright, and he had been reclining, and he said: Bring what is with you, O son of Ṣafwān.
sentences.i: He sat up, for he had been leaning back, and said, “Let me have what you have, son of Ṣafwān.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنَّ مَلِكًا مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ خَرَجَ قَبْلَكَ فِي عَامٍ قَبْلَ عَامِكَ هَذَا إِلَى هَذِهِ الْأَرْضِ فَقَالَ لِجُلَسَائِهِ هَلْ رَأَيْتُمْ مِثْلَ مَا أَنَا فِيهِ وَهَلْ أُعْطِيَ أَحَدٌ مِثْلَ مَا أَعْطَيْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā amīra al-muʾminīna inna malikan mina al-mulūki kharaja qablaka fī ʿāmin qabla ʿāmika hādhā ilā hādhihi al-arḍi fa-qāla li-julasāʾihi hal raʾaytum mithla mā anā fīhi wa-hal uʿṭiya aḥadun mithla mā aʿṭaytuhu
sentences.l: And he said: O commander of the believers, a king of the kings went out before you, in a year before this year of yours, to this land; and he said to his companions: Have you seen the like of what I am in? And has anyone been given the like of what I have been given?
sentences.i: He said, “Commander of the Faithful, a king came out to this same place before you, in a year before this one, and he said to his companions, ‘Have you ever seen the like of what I am in? Has anyone been given what I have been given?’

sentences.t: وَعِنْدَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَقَايَا حَمَلَةِ الْحُجَّةِ وَالْمُعِينِينَ عَلَى الْحَقِّ السَّالِكِينَ فِي مِنْهَاجِهِ فَقَالَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّكَ سَأَلْتَ عَنْ أَمْرٍ عَظِيمٍ أَتَأْذَنُ لِي فِي الْجَوَابِ عَنْهُ قَالَ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿindahu rajulun min baqāyā ḥamalati al-ḥujjati wa-al-muʿīnīna ʿalā al-ḥaqqi al-sālikīna fī minhājihi fa-qāla ayyuhā al-maliku innaka saʾalta ʿan amrin ʿaẓīmin a-taʾdhanu lī fī al-jawābi ʿanhu qāla naʿam
sentences.l: And with him was a man of the remnants of the bearers of the proof and the helpers upon the truth, the walkers in its path; and he said: O king, you have asked about a great matter; will you permit me to answer about it? He said: Yes.
sentences.i: Beside him was a man from what remained of those who uphold the proof and help the truth and walk in its path. He said, ‘O king, you have asked about a weighty matter. Will you let me answer?’ The king said, ‘Yes.’
sentences.n: The man belongs to the remnant of the righteous who bear “the proof” (al-ḥujja), that is, the argument of God against His creatures. Both sālikīn and minhāj are words for travelling a road, which is how the text pictures the religious life.

sentences.t: قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي أَنْتَ فِيهِ شَيْأً لَمْ يَزَلْ أَمْ شَيْأً زَائِلًا
sentences.tr: qāla a-raʾayta alladhī anta fīhi shayʾan lam yazal am shayʾan zāʾilan
sentences.l: He said: Do you see what you are in a thing that has never ceased, or a thing passing away?
sentences.i: He said, ‘Is what you have now something that will never cease, or something that is passing?’
sentences.n: The print spells شيئا as شيأ, here and just below; kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هُوَ شَيْءٌ زَائِلٌ قَالَ فَمَالِي أَرَاكَ قَدْ أُعْجِبْتَ بِشَيْءٍ تَكُونُ فِيهِ قَلِيلًا وَتُسْأَلُ عَنْهُ طَوِيلًا وَتَكُونُ عِنْدَ حِسَابِهِ مُرْتَهَنًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla huwa shayʾun zāʾilun qāla fa-mā lī arāka qad uʿjibta bi-shayʾin takūnu fīhi qalīlan wa-tusʾalu ʿanhu ṭawīlan wa-takūnu ʿinda ḥisābihi murtahanan
sentences.l: And he said: It is a passing thing. He said: Then what is it with me that I see you pleased with a thing you will be in for a little, and be questioned about for long, and be, at its reckoning, a pledge held?
sentences.i: The king said, ‘It is something passing.’ ‘Then why do I see you so delighted with a thing you will have for a little while, be questioned about for a long one, and be held in pledge for when it is reckoned?’
sentences.n: Murtahan, “held as a pledge,” is the person kept in hock for a debt: the king will answer for his wealth at the reckoning on the Day of Judgement.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَأَيْنَ الْمَهْرَبُ وَأَيْنَ الْمَطْلَبُ
sentences.tr: qāla fa-ayna al-mahrabu wa-ayna al-maṭlabu
sentences.l: He said: Then where is the escape, and where the goal?
sentences.i: He said, ‘Then where is the way of escape, and where is the thing to seek?’

sentences.t: قَالَ أَنْ تُقِيمَ فِي مُلْكِكَ فَتَعْمَلَ عَلَى طَاعَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى أَوْ تَلْبَسَ أَطْمَارَكَ وَتَعْبُدَ رَبَّكَ حَتَّي يَأْتِيَكَ أَجَلُكَ فَإِذَا كَانَ السَّحَرُ فَإِنِّي قَادِمٌ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: qāla an tuqīma fī mulkika fa-taʿmala ʿalā ṭāʿati Allāhi taʿālā aw talbasa aṭmāraka wa-taʿbuda rabbaka ḥattā yatiyaka ajaluka fa-idhā kāna al-saḥaru fa-innī qādimun ʿalayka
sentences.l: He said: That you stay in your kingdom and work upon the obedience of God, the exalted, or put on your rags and worship your Lord until your appointed hour comes to you. And when it is the dawn, I shall come to you.
sentences.i: He said, ‘Either stay in your kingdom and work in obedience to God Most High, or put on your rags and worship your Lord until your appointed time comes. When it is dawn, I will come to you.’
sentences.n: Aṭmār, “rags,” is the ascetic's patched garment. The print writes حتي with a dotted final yāʾ.

sentences.t: قَالَ خَالِدُ بْنُ صَفْوَانَ ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ قَرَعَ عَلَيْهِ بَابَهُ عِنْدَ السَّحَرِ فَإِذَا هُوَ قَدْ وَضَعَ تَاجَهُ وَتَهَيَّأَ لِلسِّيَاحَةِ مِنْ عِظَمِ مَوْعِظَتِهِ
sentences.tr: qāla Khālidu ibnu Ṣafwāna thumma inna al-rajula qaraʿa ʿalayhi bābahu ʿinda al-saḥari fa-idhā huwa qad waḍaʿa tājahu wa-tahayyaʾa li-al-siyāḥati min ʿiẓami mawʿiẓatihi
sentences.l: Khālid ibn Ṣafwān said: Then the man knocked at his door at the dawn, and behold, he had put down his crown and made ready for wandering, from the greatness of his admonition.
sentences.i: Khālid ibn Ṣafwān said: At dawn the man knocked at the king's door, and there was the king, his crown laid aside and ready to set out as a wanderer, so great had been the warning he was given.
sentences.n: Siyāḥa, “wandering,” is the ascetic's life on the road, giving up a settled place.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى هِشَامُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بُكَاءً كَثِيرًا حَتَّى بَلَّ لِحْيَتَهُ وَأَمَرَ بِنَزْعِ مَا عَلَيْهِ وَلَزِمَ قَصْرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-bakā Hishāmu ibnu ʿAbdi al-Maliki bukāʾan kathīran ḥattā balla liḥyatahu wa-amara bi-nazʿi mā ʿalayhi wa-lazima qaṣrahu
sentences.l: And Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik wept much weeping until he wet his beard, and commanded the taking off of what was on him, and kept to his palace.
sentences.i: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik wept long, until his beard was wet, and ordered his finery taken off him, and he stayed in his palace.

sentences.t: فَأَتَتِ الْمَوَالِي وَالْخَدَمُ إِلَى خَالِدِ بْنِ صَفْوَانَ وَقَالُوا أَهَكَذَا فَعَلْتَ بِا مِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَفْسَدْتَ لَذَّتَهُ وَنَغَّصْتَ حَيَاتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-atati al-mawālī wa-al-khadamu ilā Khālidi ibni Ṣafwāna wa-qālū a-hakadhā faʿalta bi-[a]mīri al-muʾminīna afsadta ladhdhatahu wa-naghghaṣta ḥayātahu
sentences.l: And the clients and the servants came to Khālid ibn Ṣafwān and said: Is it thus you have done with the commander of the believers? You have spoiled his pleasure and soured his life.
sentences.i: The freedmen and servants came to Khālid ibn Ṣafwān and said, “Is this what you have done to the Commander of the Faithful? You have ruined his pleasure and soured his life!”
sentences.n: The print separates the preposition from the noun (با مير, for بأمير); kept as printed. Mawālī are the freedmen and clients attached to a great household.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ قَالَتْ لِشَرْكَانَ وَكَمْ فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ مِنَ النَّصَائِحِ إِنِّي لَأَعْجِزُ عَنِ الْإِتْيَانِ بِجَمِيعِ مَا فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ فِي مَجْلِسٍ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Nuzhata al-Zamāni qālat li-Sharkāna wa-kam fī hādhā al-bābi mina al-naṣāʾiḥi innī la-aʿjizu ʿani al-ityāni bi-jamīʿi mā fī hādhā al-bābi fī majlisin wāḥidin
sentences.l: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said to Sharkān: And how many counsels there are in this chapter! I am unable to bring all that is in this chapter in one sitting.
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said to Sharkān, “How many words of counsel there are in this chapter! I could not give you everything in it in a single sitting.”

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night. The print's last word is damaged (الم—باح, with a dash inside it) and ends in a stray dash; it is read as the formula's usual al-mubāḥ.
